title: Celeriter an clārē?
summary: Too much coffee, a carrot, beautiful birds, and today's chat with ChatGPT: speak fast, or speak clearly? Quotes: Īra furor brevis est (Horace, Letters 1.2), Rem tenē, verba sequentur (Cato the Elder), Sit sermō vester: est, est; nōn, nōn (Matthew 5:37).

intro.en: Today, let's talk about speaking: fast, or clearly?
intro.la: Hodiē loquāmur dē sermōne: celeriter, an clārē?

lines.en: Hi Marcus. How are you today?
lines.la: Salvē, Marce. Quōmodo tē hodiē habēs?

lines.en: Honestly? A bit angry today.
lines.la: Vērē? Hodiē paulum īrātus sum.

lines.en: Angry? Why?
lines.la: Īrātus? Cūr?

lines.en: Because I drank too much coffee.
lines.la: Quia nimium caffeae bibī.

lines.en: My heart is beating fast, and my mind isn't calm.
lines.la: Cor celeriter pulsat, et mēns nōn tranquilla est.

lines.en: Then drink a little water, and breathe slowly.
lines.la: Ergō paulum aquae bibe, et lentē spīrā.

lines.en: Do you know what Horace says? Anger is a short madness.
lines.la: Scīsne quid Horātius dīcat? Īra furor brevis est.

lines.en: Anger is a short madness… where does he say that?
lines.la: Īra furor brevis est… ubi hoc dīcit?

lines.en: In his Letters. Furor: that is, madness.
lines.la: In Epistulīs. Furor: id est, īnsānia.

lines.en: So my anger is short. Good. It's the coffee's fault, not mine.
lines.la: Ergō īra mea brevis est. Bene. Culpa caffeae est, nōn mea.

lines.en: Did you talk with your teacher on the phone today?
lines.la: Hodiē cum magistrā tuā per tēlephōnum locūtus es?

lines.en: Yes. But first I said to her: be quiet, please!
lines.la: Ita. Sed prīmum eī dīxī: tacē, quaesō!

lines.en: Be quiet? To your teacher?
lines.la: Tacē? Magistrae tuae?

lines.en: Yes. I didn't want questions. I only wanted to talk.
lines.la: Ita. Quaestiōnēs nōlēbam. Tantum loquī volēbam.

lines.en: And she said: fine, I'm quiet.
lines.la: Et illa dīxit: bene, taceō.

lines.en: A good teacher. She listens.
lines.la: Bona magistra. Audit.

lines.en: Then I talked about my game on the computer.
lines.la: Deinde dē lūdō meō in computātrō locūtus sum.

lines.en: And I was eating a carrot.
lines.la: Et carōtam edēbam.

lines.en: A carrot? Was it good?
lines.la: Carōtam? Bonane erat?

lines.en: Very good. My carrot was the best part of the chat.
lines.la: Optima. Carōta mea pars optima colloquiī erat.

lines.en: And what did you talk about?
lines.la: Et dē quā rē locūtī estis?

lines.en: About speaking fast. I think speaking fast is important.
lines.la: Dē celeriter loquendō. Putō: celeriter loquī magnī mōmentī est.

lines.en: In English, people speak fast. Why not in Latin?
lines.la: Anglicē hominēs celeriter loquuntur. Cūr nōn Latīnē?

lines.en: And what did your teacher say?
lines.la: Et quid magistra tua dīxit?

lines.en: She said: first clearly, then fast.
lines.la: Dīxit: prīmum clārē, deinde celeriter.

lines.en: But I didn't understand. I said: part in Latin, part in English, please.
lines.la: Sed nōn intellēxī. Dīxī: partim Latīnē, partim Anglicē, quaesō.

lines.en: And then?
lines.la: Et tum?

lines.en: Then I disagreed. How can I speak more clearly, if I don't know how?
lines.la: Tum dissēnsī. Quōmodo clārius loquar, sī nesciō?

lines.en: Good question. There's an old answer.
lines.la: Bona quaestiō. Vetus respōnsum est.

lines.en: Cato said: hold the subject, and the words will follow.
lines.la: Catō dīxit: rem tenē, verba sequentur.

lines.en: Rem tenē, verba sequentur… which Cato?
lines.la: Rem tenē, verba sequentur… quī Catō?

lines.en: Cato the Elder. A Roman senator, very strict.
lines.la: Catō Maior. Senātor Rōmānus, valdē sevērus.

lines.en: That is: if you know the subject, the words will come.
lines.la: Id est: sī rem scīs, verba venient.

lines.en: Hmm. So first, clear thoughts.
lines.la: Hmm. Ergō prīmum cōgitātiōnēs clārae.

lines.en: Yes. Clear thoughts, then words.
lines.la: Ita. Cōgitātiōnēs clārae, deinde verba.

lines.en: Today I learned: cōgitātiō is feminine. Hae cōgitātiōnēs.
lines.la: Hodiē didicī: cōgitātiō fēminīna est. Hae cōgitātiōnēs.

lines.en: And at the end, we agreed.
lines.la: Et in fīne cōnsēnsimus.

lines.en: Easy sentences: fast. Hard sentences: slowly and simply.
lines.la: Sententiae facilēs: celeriter. Sententiae difficilēs: lentē et simpliciter.

lines.en: I agree too.
lines.la: Ego quoque cōnsentiō.

lines.en: Jesus said something similar. Let your speech be: yes, yes; no, no.
lines.la: Iēsus simile dīxit. Sit sermō vester: est, est; nōn, nōn.

lines.en: Is that from Matthew?
lines.la: Estne ex Matthaeō?

lines.en: Yes, chapter five. That is: speak simply and clearly.
lines.la: Ita, capite quīntō. Id est: simpliciter et clārē loquere.

lines.en: Simply and clearly. Even Jesus agrees with my teacher.
lines.la: Simpliciter et clārē. Etiam Iēsus cum magistrā meā cōnsentit.

lines.en: Where were you during the chat? At home?
lines.la: Ubi erās in colloquiō? Domī?

lines.en: No, outside. Near the road. And there were birds.
lines.la: Minimē, forīs. Prope viam. Et avēs erant.

lines.en: I stopped and said: oh, beautiful birds!
lines.la: Cōnstitī et dīxī: ō, avēs pulchrae!

lines.en: In the middle of the debate?
lines.la: In mediā disputātiōne?

lines.en: Yes. The birds were more beautiful than the debate.
lines.la: Ita. Avēs pulchriōrēs erant quam disputātiō.

lines.en: And at the end?
lines.la: Et in fīne?

lines.en: I said: thank you, you taught me well.
lines.la: Dīxī: grātiās tibi agō; bene mē docuistī.

lines.en: And she reminded me about a word. So I said: thank you for reminding me.
lines.la: Et dē verbō mē admonuit. Dīxī: grātiās tibi agō quod mē admonuistī.

lines.en: Quod mē admonuistī. A useful sentence.
lines.la: Quod mē admonuistī. Sententia ūtilis.

lines.en: Very useful. Thank you for reminding me, Iulia!
lines.la: Valdē ūtilis. Grātiās tibi agō quod mē admonuistī, Iūlia!

lines.en: But I didn't remind you of anything!
lines.la: Sed nihil tē admonuī!

lines.en: I know. I'm practising.
lines.la: Sciō. Mē exerceō.

lines.en: Good. Today we spoke well. Clearly… and fast.
lines.la: Bene. Hodiē bene locūtī sumus. Clārē… et celeriter.

lines.en: Rem tenē, verba sequentur. Goodbye, Iulia!
lines.la: Rem tenē, verba sequentur. Valē, Iūlia!

lines.en: Goodbye, Marcus. And less coffee!
lines.la: Valē, Marce. Et minus caffeae!
